newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open flat to down.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open flat to down.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open flat to lower Tuesday as the financial markets awaited key U.S economic data.
March U.S. consumer prices are due to be released at 0830 EDT, with analysts forecasting a hike of 0.2 percent in the overall figure compared to a 0.3 percent advance in February.
COMEX June gold was called $0.50 to $1.00 weaker from Monday's close of $348.70 an ounce after trading from $348.50 to $347.80 on ACCESS.
COMEX May silver was called flat to 2.0 cents lower.
The gold market was still under pressure overnight, with further testing of support levels expected.
In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted at $345.70/$346.20 early against the London morning fix of $345.60 and the New York June gold close Monday at $348.70.
COMEX gold stocks were unchanged at 1,032,382 ounces Monday.
COMEX silver stocks fell 113,152 ounces to 190,537,309 ounces Monday.
NYMEX July platinum was called $0.50 to $1.00, with NYMEX June palladium called flat to off $0.50 cents.
In addition to the consumer prices, business inventories for February, forecast to rise 0.2 percent, are also due at 0830.
Real earnings for March were due at 1000, with the Redbook for week ended April 12, scheduled for 1455.
